beats.summary: Robert forbids Harry and Dwight from contacting the big client Prestige until he decides how to divide the Binghamton accounts.

evidence.snippet: I have decided. Neither of you are to have any contact with either Prestige or any other Binghamton client until I have figured out how to divide things up.
Dwight: Prestige is ours. Okay, they're responsible for half of the junk mail on the eastern seaboard. We get them.

beats.summary: Andy tries to meet with the CEO Mr. Ramish to pitch his paper business and offers personal attention and a house key.

evidence.snippet: Andy: I'm a former paper executive. I know the product. I know the margins. I can save you 25% on your costs.
Andy: Of course they have. Which is why I'm giving you a key to my house. Whatever you need – anytime, night or day – you just stop on by.

beats.summary: Dwight and Jim attempt to sabotage Robert by slashing his tires and then try to escape Harry by activating the elevator seismic failsafe, but Dwight's pants fall down.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: Go slash his tires! Go dent his hood.
Dwight: I'm gonna activate the seismic failsafe. We'll be stuck between floors for hours. Oh. My pants fell down.

beats.summary: Robert compares shaping a company to training a geisha and delays making a decision about the big client.

evidence.snippet: Robert: Shaping a company is, in a sense, similar to training a geisha. You have to mold not merely the physical form, but also the character.

beats.summary: Angela is sent by Robert to take over if Pam fails, and the office engages in light girl talk with Gabe.

evidence.snippet: Gabe: Sometimes I wonder if I have ovaries in my scrotum, because I am great at girl talk.
